## Dependencies that changed after your training data

Your training data (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, cutoff 2026-06-30) predates the versions this project pins. When a note below conflicts with what you remember, follow the note: it describes the installed version. Tags: [types] = diff of the published type declarations, [changelog] = release notes, [guide] = the package's upgrade guide, [summary] = summary of both.

**typescript** 6.0.3 → 7.0.2 (major)
- `CompilerOptions` options removed: `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`, `alwaysStrict`, `baseUrl`, `charset`, `downlevelIteration`, `importsNotUsedAsValues`, `keyofStringsOnly`, `noStrictGenericChecks` (+7 more). [types]
- `CompilerOptions` moved to `typescript/unstable/sync` [types]

**zod** 4.4.3 → 4.6.7
- The pattern string is user-visible, and every copy of it changes: `z.regexes.email`, which has no capture groups now — neither of the two it used to expose held a usable value; `issue.pattern` on a failed `z.email()`; and the `pattern` tha… [changelog]
- Defaults inside optional fields are now applied, so `z.string().default("tuna").optional()` turns `{}` into `{ a: "tuna" }`. Code that checks whether a key exists may break. [guide]
- `z.base64url()` now rejects padded input. Strip the `=` padding before validating. [guide]
- `z.string().ipv6()` now validates with `new URL()`, so some previously accepted values fail. Note that `.ip()` and `.cidr()` are gone; use `z.union([z.ipv4(), z.ipv6()])` instead. [guide]
- `z.emoji()` no longer backtracks exponentially on a failed match . [changelog]
- The runtime patterns for `z.base64()` and `z.base64url()` are the character sets, with length and padding enforced in code, so a multi-megabyte string can no longer overflow the regex stack through a composed schema. The JSON Schema output… [changelog]
- Each check used to write its own bounds into the schema as it attached, in chain order, so a format check applied after `.min()` and `.max()` replaced the tighter values with its own range. The converter folds the checks as a conjunction n… [changelog]
- Separately, an `unrecognized_keys` issue no longer aborts the schema it came from, so a strict object with an extra key *and* a bad value now reports both issues instead of just the first. [changelog]
